A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WildChat-50M and RE-WILD study. Their text, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including the retained output samples and v2's new Appendix F.

before.justification: V1 reports original SFT benchmark evaluations, data-scaling and model-blending experiments, throughput measurements, response-similarity analyses, and qualitative output comparisons.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative observations about problems encountered during synthetic-data generation.

M1.justification: The response-generation pipeline, three-source RE-WILD mixture in Table 1, and SFT procedure remain unchanged. Clarifications about model variants and Appendix F's recommendations do not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WildChat prompts, RE-WILD training sources, and nine evaluation benchmarks. Neither the expanded WildChat-1M discussion nor Appendix F establishes additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains Tulu 3 SFT, Magpie Align SFT, and UltraChat as baselines. Comparator membership in the DGM, model-family, judge-preference, and blending comparisons also remains unchanged; the changed Command R+ citation does not introduce a different comparator.

E3.justification: The training budgets, 100k/250k/500k scaling conditions, evaluation metrics, judge configuration, and existing ablation procedures are retained. V2's additional setup explanations do not establish a protocol revision; the added confidence intervals concern uncertainty reporting.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds an informal analysis of generation failures, reporting unusable outputs from malformed system instructions and differing response lengths under identical token limits. This is limited qualitative evidence, without a controlled new ablation. Existing quantitative analyses and Appendix E's output examples are retained.

E5.justification: V2 substantially expands uncertainty reporting by adding intervals to seven benchmark columns throughout Tables 2, 6, and 7, described in Section 3.1 as normal-approximation 95% confidence intervals. V1 provided point estimates in those tables, although Table 5 already included response-similarity standard deviations. No additional runs or seeds are reported.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged after matching scaling and rounding; for example, Q72's Table 2 BBH score changes from 48.07 to 0.48. Appendix F newly reports qualitative observations about temperature-related defects, formatting failures, tokenization effects, and claimed bias mitigation through DGM diversity, without quantitative supporting results.

T1.justification: The existing metric descriptions, proportional-frequency definition, and agreement criterion remain unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical proofs, and v2's confidence-interval statement adds statistical reporting rather than a mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the WildChat-50M dataset, comparative DGM analysis, and RE-WILD outperforming Tulu-3 with approximately 40% as many samples. The conclusions concerning DGM choice, stylistic inheritance, and response similarity are retained.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 replaces the broad inference that SDQ primarily depends on prompt diversity with a more specific interpretation that prompt-diversity benefits do not extend to response diversity. It also acknowledges the limited scope of same-family learning experiments. Appendix F adds explanations of bias transfer and generation failures, alongside mitigation recommendations.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the availability statement from some artifacts being available and others forthcoming to all artifacts being available, and explicitly identifies the base model for the main method/baseline setup. Appendix F adds accounts of batch restarts and model-specific token-limit calibration, plus practical generation guidance, without supplying complete per-model configurations.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds a paragraph explaining WildChat-1M's collection process and positioning WildChat-50M as a complementary source of synthetic responses. The Command R+ reference changes from Duran et al. to Gomez's model announcement. The additional WildChat bibliography entry represents an already cited work.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording corrections and clarifications, expands the related-work discussion, and appends the practical-guidance section. The main section order and most of the existing narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 reformats the title and affiliation information, adds running headers, and compacts Tables 2, 6, and 7 to accommodate uncertainty entries, with additional bold highlighting. Table 4 moves from page 7 to page 8. All four figures and seven tables are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through confidence intervals for existing benchmark comparisons, a qualification of the limited same-family evidence, and clearer documentation and research positioning. Appendix F provides practical context, but its new bias-mitigation and temperature claims lack quantified supporting analyses. These limitations temper the gains, while the core empirical evidence remains stable.
